div.l: For sawcefleem he was with eyen narwe
As hoot he was and leccherous as a sparwe
With scalled browes blak and piled berd
Of his visage children were afferd
Ther nas quik siluer litarge nor brimston
Borace ceruse ne oyle of trarter non
Ne oynement that wolde clense and byte
That him myghte helpe of his whilkes whyte
Nor of the knobbes sittynge in his chekes
Wel loued he garleek oynons and leekes
And for to drinke strong wyn rede as blood
Than wolde he speke and crie as he were wood
For whan that he wel dronken hadde the wyn
Than wolde he speke no word but latyn
A fewe termes hadde he two or thre
That he hadde y lerned out of som decre
No wonder is he herde it al the day
And eek ȝe knowen wel how þat a iay
Can clepe watte as wel as can the pope
But who so couthe in other þing hym grope
Than hadde he spent al his philosophie
Ay questio quid iuris wolde he crie
He was a gentil harlot and a kynde
A better felawe shulde men not fynde
He wolde suffre for a quart of wyn
A good felawe to haue his concubyn
A twelf monthe and excuse him atte fulle
Ful pⁱriuely eke a fynche couthe he pulle
And ȝif he fond owher a good felawe
He wolde techen him to haue non awe
In such cas of the erchedekenes curs
But ȝif a mannes soule were in his purs
For in his purs he shulde punisshed be
Purs is the erchedekenes helle seide he
But wel I woot he lyed right in dede
Of cursyng oughte ech gilty man to drede
For curs wol sleen right assoilyng saueth
And also war him of a significauit
In daunger hadde he athis owne gyse
